title: The Detective
build: T64 tape image of a cracked release: the game packed into one 44,302-byte program (Trianon, 1987), and a second program of crackers' instructions (Danish Gold, 1987)

tools.emulator: own build of github.com/barryw/vice-mcp, release v3.13.2, commit 1e83aab134

exclude: runtime: zero page, the game's variables, cleared by the cold start ($2048) and written as it runs
runtime: the sprite slot tables ($0208-$0264), the typed-line and list buffer ($0300) and the mirror index tables ($0380, $03C0, built by $919E)
runtime: the message bar's line buffer ($21D8 writes it, $2B21 reads it)
runtime: the multicolour mirror table built at start-up by $2383
runtime: the music player's spare byte ($0600) and the save areas for the picture behind each door ($0610 on, $3A27)
not the game's: what the crackers' unpacker left in memory, text of another program ("TOWN RESCUE", "KASSETTE OHNE HIGHSCORE"); no instruction of the game names it
runtime: the room map, 15 rows of 256 columns, built for each room by $388D (and the title's tables at $0C00-$0FFF, built by $8DC0)

runtime: the room's door lists ($1CC0-$1CFF, built by $388D), the music player's state ($1CE8-$1D1F), and the player's, the cast's and the game's state ($1D41-$1EDF), set at the start of each game and written as it runs
unused: fourteen bytes before the flip flags at $3FF0 that no instruction reads
runtime: the cast's flip flags ($3FF0-$3FF9) and the number of the room character set in place ($3FFF)
runtime: the buffer where a sprite shape is mirrored ($91E0) or a portrait wiped on ($8B01), inside the sprite shapes
runtime: the screen and the sprite pointers, drawn by the game
runtime: the NMI, reset and IRQ vectors, written by $28FA
include: the RAM under the I/O area: room pictures 5 to 13 of the list at $C100, which $3BD7 unpacks with the I/O banked out ($01 = $34)

regions: the engine: start-up, interrupts, text, menus, rooms and doors
the title's character set at the hand-over; the room set in play
the text panel's character set, with the word list for speech and the objects' starting places
sprite shapes: the cast, the player, portraits, pointer and props
the adventure module: menus, objects, speech, music and actions
the nine characters' scripts, in the interpreter's byte code
the module's last routines: questions, the arrest, keyboard and storm
animation frames, the safe's pictures and room tables
the room character sets, swapped in by the title and per room
